# Perch

*Pigeon Keeper*

|  |  |

## Personality

Soft-spoken, patient and covered in feathers. Perch understands birds better than people and admits it.

## Lore

Perch lives at the top of the city, in a pigeon loft on the highest roof in Urbanograd, and comes down as seldom as possible. The loft sits on the Crooked Tower, the tallest and leanest of Old Grad's fortress towers, and the climb to it would wind most people half Perch's age. Perch is seventy-one, soft-spoken and patient, and nearly always dusted with feathers. Perch understands birds better than people and says so without embarrassment, because it is simply true.

### A life with birds

Perch was born in a stacked house below the tower and began feeding the old loft's birds as a child, when an elderly keeper named Isolde Spurr still ran it. Isolde taught Perch to read a pigeon's mood from the set of its wings and to tell every bird apart by its call. When Isolde died, Perch was twenty and already doing most of the work, so the loft simply became Perch's. That was fifty-one years ago.

The birds carry short messages to other towns and back: orders for goods, news of births and deaths, notes between friends who cannot make the journey. Rooftop runners like Kite carry messages within the city; Perch's birds carry them beyond it. Each bird is trained to one or two homes, and Perch knows which is which the way other people know their neighbours' faces.

### The list

A few years ago, a steady old bird named Greyfeather refused to fly a route she had flown a hundred times. She circled the tower once and came straight back. Perch thought she was ill. Then another bird refused, and another, always on routes that cross certain stretches of wild country. Since then Perch has kept a careful list: which bird, which route, which day, which way the wind blew. The list is long now. Some routes the birds will still fly in the morning but not at dusk. A few they will not fly at all.

Perch does not know why. Perch has guesses, and keeps them modest. Starling, who stargazes on a nearby roof and sometimes sees the horizon toward the middle of the island flicker, has begun bringing a notebook of dates to the loft, and the two of them sit with their lists side by side late at night, not quite saying what they are both wondering.

### Neighbours

Lux, the Keeper of the Lanterns, is Perch's closest friend. Both of them spend their evenings higher than anyone else in the city, and Lux often stops at the loft on the way down from the towers to share a pot of tea and a report of which lanterns are out. Old Parsnip gardens on the next roof over and trades cabbage leaves for pigeon droppings, which he insists are better than gold for his tubs. Pounce, a large grey cat nobody invited, sleeps in the loft every day. The pigeons have accepted him with deep reluctance, and Perch suspects he has never once tried to catch one because it would be too much effort.

### Hopes and fears

Perch wants the birds to fly freely again, and fears the day the last open route closes and the loft goes quiet. Perch also worries, privately, about who will keep the birds afterwards; no young person has yet asked to learn.

A quest might carry a message the birds refuse to take, find out what waits along one of the refused routes, or find Perch an apprentice who listens to birds.
